=== cli-text-claude
Claude Code
a Claude Pro or Max account (a paid plan)
claude verification failed. Re-run install.sh to retry the login.
7bc073a606abe82414e8d5d3dc791e50  -
[rc=0]
=== cli-login-claude
You will sign in with your Claude Pro or Max account.

  1. Claude prints a long link. Open it in your browser
     (touch and hold the link to copy it).
  2. Sign in and tap Authorize.
  3. The page shows a code. Copy it.
  4. Come back here, paste the code at the prompt that
     says "Paste code here" and press Enter ONCE.

Claude also says "Opening browser". Ignore that line:
this box has no screen, so nothing opens.

Do not press Enter again until you have the code.

Press Enter to get your sign-in link.

https://claude.invalid/oauth/authorize?x=1
Paste code here if prompted > [code=]

[rc=0]
=== cli-text-antigravity
Antigravity (agy)
a Google account
agy login could not be verified. To retry: re-run 'sudo /opt/buildersinabox/payload/install.sh' and complete the Google OAuth (choose 'Google OAuth', paste the authorization code). If it keeps failing, confirm you finished the sign-in in the browser — a successful login writes a token to ~builder/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token.
7bc073a606abe82414e8d5d3dc791e50  -
[rc=0]
=== cli-login-antigravity
Antigravity (agy) signs in on its own screen. You will
need a Google account. When it opens:

  1. Choose the login menu entry:  Google OAuth
  2. agy prints a long sign-in link. Touch and hold it to
     copy it (it may wrap over several lines: copy it
     all), open it in your browser and sign in.
  3. Paste the authorization code it gives you back into
     agy.
  4. agy may ask a few setup questions (colour,
     telemetry, trust this folder). Accept the defaults.
  5. Back at the agy prompt, type  /quit  (or Ctrl+D) to
     hand control back to the setup.

When you leave agy, the setup checks the login and goes on.
Press Enter to launch agy.
agy tui
[rc=0]
=== cli-text-codex
Codex
a ChatGPT account
codex login could not be verified. Most often the ChatGPT 'device code login' toggle is still off — enable it (ChatGPT → Settings → Security) and re-run 'sudo /opt/buildersinabox/payload/install.sh'. Fallbacks: forward Codex's local login port over SSH and log in normally ('ssh -L 1455:localhost:1455 builder@<box>' then 'codex login'), or set an API key with 'codex login --api-key'. A successful login writes a token to ~builder/.codex/auth.json.
7bc073a606abe82414e8d5d3dc791e50  -
[rc=0]
=== cli-login-codex
Codex signs in with your ChatGPT account, using a device
code. First, in your browser:

  1. Open ChatGPT > Settings > Security and turn ON
     "device code login" (also called "device
     authorization"). Without it the login is refused.

Then we start the login here:

  2. This screen prints a link and a short code.
  3. Open the link in a real browser (Chrome or Safari),
     not in the ChatGPT app. Sign in, type the code and
     approve. There is no QR code in this flow.
  4. When you approve, this screen notices by itself: there
     is nothing to paste back here.

Press Enter to start the Codex login.
codex login stub
[rc=0]
=== cli-text-opencode
OpenCode
an OpenCode key, or another AI provider account
OpenCode is not logged in yet. To log in later: connect to the box as builder, run 'opencode auth login', choose OpenCode Go or Zen and paste your key from https://opencode.ai/auth, then run 'biab' to continue the setup.
7bc073a606abe82414e8d5d3dc791e50  -
[rc=0]
=== cli-login-opencode
OpenCode signs in from its own menu. Before it opens:

  1. In your browser, open  https://opencode.ai/auth ,
     sign in, add your billing details and copy your API
     key (OpenCode Go or Zen). Prefer another provider
     you already pay for? Choose it in the menu instead.
  2. We start OpenCode's login now. Choose OpenCode Go or
     OpenCode Zen and paste the key when it asks.
  3. When it says the credential was saved, the setup
     goes on by itself.

Press Enter to start the OpenCode login.
<W>/stubs/sudo: line 3: /usr/local/bin/opencode: No such file or directory

OpenCode is not logged in yet. To log in later: connect to the box as builder, run 'opencode auth login', choose OpenCode Go or Zen and paste your key from https://opencode.ai/auth, then run 'biab' to continue the setup.
[rc=78]

=== cli-first-prompt
This is the first message on a brand-new Builders in a Box, and I may never have used anything like it. Run the tutorial skill and guide me through it, with these rules for your very first reply. One: welcome me in a few short lines. Say what this box is (a private computer that builds software with me and that I control from my phone), what the setup just installed (my AI, a private link to my devices, a workspace with ready-made skills) and what the next 10 minutes look like (connect GitHub, pick a first project, create it, a short tour). Two: always tell me what you are about to do, and why, before you do it, and wait for my go-ahead before anything that changes the box. Three: keep every message short and end it with one question. Four: read the install profile in /var/lib/buildersinabox/state.json so you call this machine by the right name.[rc=0]

Step 3 of 6 - Continue remotely
######......  About 4 minutes left

Use your laptop for the rest of setup.

1. Install Tailscale.
   Sign in with the same account:

https://tailscale.com/download

2. Open its terminal and connect:

ssh builder@biabox

If that name does not work, use:

ssh builder@100.64.1.2

3. In the SSH session, run:

biab

=== ssh-cloud-notice

Step 3 of 6 - Check how you connect
######......  About a moment left

Your cloud provider manages SSH on this server
(provider-managed). Builders in a Box does not change it:
no password login is added and no SSH setting is touched.

Port 22 may still be open to the internet. Closing it is
done in your provider's console, later, once you are sure
the app works.

Done: SSH is left as your provider set it.

Press Enter to continue.
[rc=0]
=== ssh-hold-open-1


  SSH is still open to the internet on this box
  ------------------------------------

This machine is reachable over SSH from 203.0.113.9, which is OUTSIDE
your Tailscale network — and there is no SSH key on file yet, so a password
is the only way in. Disabling it now would lock you out, so Builders in a
Box has NOT marked SSH as secured on this box.

What this means: until you close it, anyone on the internet can try to
brute-force your password over SSH.

To close it, do EITHER of these:

  1. Reconnect to this box over Tailscale, then run:
       ssh builder@100.64.1.2      # verify tailnet reachability
       sudo BIB_SSH_FORCE_TAILSCALE=1 \
           /opt/buildersinabox/payload/wizard/35-ssh-finalize.sh
     (binds sshd to your private Tailscale address only)

  2. Finish /tutorial in the Claude Code app — Beat 2 imports your GitHub
     SSH key and closes this automatically.

Recovery if you ever get locked out is documented in ~/README.md
("If SSH ever fails") and SECURITY.md.
I understand my SSH is still exposed to the internet with a password. What now?
  Choose one
  1  reconnect-over-tailscale-first
  2  I-understand-continue-exposed-for-now
  Type a number
  Your choice [reconnect-over-tailscale-first] > [rc=0]

=== ssh-reconnect


  SSH hardened to key-only (still reachable, not yet tailnet-only)
  ------------------------------------

You're connected from outside your Tailscale network, so SSH still listens
on the public interface — but password login is now OFF, so it can't be
brute-forced (key-only).

To finish locking SSH to your private Tailscale address only, reconnect over
Tailscale first (so you can't get locked out), then run:

    ssh builder@100.64.1.2      # verify tailnet reachability
    sudo BIB_SSH_FORCE_TAILSCALE=1 \
        /opt/buildersinabox/payload/wizard/35-ssh-finalize.sh

Recovery if you get locked out is in ~/README.md ("If SSH ever fails")
and SECURITY.md.
[rc=0]

Now you sign in to Claude Code, so the AI
on this box works for your account.

You will need:
  a Claude Pro or Max account (a paid plan)

You will sign in with your Claude Pro or Max account.

  1. Claude prints a long link. Open it in your browser
     (touch and hold the link to copy it).
  2. Sign in and tap Authorize.
  3. The page shows a code. Copy it.
  4. Come back here, paste the code at the prompt that
     says "Paste code here" and press Enter ONCE.

Claude also says "Opening browser". Ignore that line:
this box has no screen, so nothing opens.

Do not press Enter again until you have the code.

=== login-step-antigravity-ok

Step 4 of 6 - Connect your AI
########....  About 3 minutes left

Now you sign in to Antigravity (agy), so the AI
on this box works for your account.

You will need:
  a Google account

Antigravity (agy) signs in on its own screen. You will
need a Google account. When it opens:

  1. Choose the login menu entry:  Google OAuth
  2. agy prints a long sign-in link. Touch and hold it to
     copy it (it may wrap over several lines: copy it
     all), open it in your browser and sign in.
  3. Paste the authorization code it gives you back into
     agy.
  4. agy may ask a few setup questions (colour,
     telemetry, trust this folder). Accept the defaults.
  5. Back at the agy prompt, type  /quit  (or Ctrl+D) to
     hand control back to the setup.

When you leave agy, the setup checks the login and goes on.
Press Enter to launch agy.
agy tui

If it keeps failing, confirm you finished the sign-in in the browser — a successful login writes a token to ~builder/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token.

=== login-step-codex-ok

Step 4 of 6 - Connect your AI
########....  About 3 minutes left

Now you sign in to Codex, so the AI
on this box works for your account.

You will need:
  a ChatGPT account

Codex signs in with your ChatGPT account, using a device
code. First, in your browser:

  1. Open ChatGPT > Settings > Security and turn ON
     "device code login" (also called "device
     authorization"). Without it the login is refused.

Then we start the login here:

  2. This screen prints a link and a short code.
  3. Open the link in a real browser (Chrome or Safari),
     not in the ChatGPT app. Sign in, type the code and
     approve. There is no QR code in this flow.
  4. When you approve, this screen notices by itself: there
     is nothing to paste back here.

Press Enter to start the Codex login.
codex login stub
[TS] ERROR: codex login could not be verified. Most often the ChatGPT 'device code login' toggle is still off — enable it (ChatGPT → Settings → Security) and re-run 'sudo /opt/buildersinabox/payload/install.sh'. Fallbacks: forward Codex's local login port over SSH and log in normally ('ssh -L 1455:localhost:1455 builder@<box>' then 'codex login'), or set an API key with 'codex login --api-key'. A successful login writes a token to ~builder/.codex/auth.json.
[rc=1]

=== login-step-opencode-ok

Step 4 of 6 - Connect your AI
########....  About 3 minutes left

Now you sign in to OpenCode, so the AI
on this box works for your account.

You will need:
  an OpenCode key, or another AI provider account

OpenCode signs in from its own menu. Before it opens:

  1. In your browser, open  https://opencode.ai/auth ,
     sign in, add your billing details and copy your API
     key (OpenCode Go or Zen). Prefer another provider
     you already pay for? Choose it in the menu instead.
  2. We start OpenCode's login now. Choose OpenCode Go or
     OpenCode Zen and paste the key when it asks.
  3. When it says the credential was saved, the setup
     goes on by itself.

Press Enter to start the OpenCode login.
<W>/stubs/sudo: line 3: /usr/local/bin/opencode: No such file or directory

OpenCode is not logged in yet. To log in later: connect to the box as builder, run 'opencode auth login', choose OpenCode Go or Zen and paste your key from https://opencode.ai/auth, then run 'biab' to continue the setup.
[rc=78]

=== install-usage
Usage: sudo install.sh [options]

Options:
  --ai=<claude|antigravity|codex|opencode>  Pick the AI to install (default: claude).
  --flavor=<default|gift>    Pick the copy/banner flavor (default: default).
  --profile=<dedicated|cloud>  Who owns SSH on this box (default: dedicated).
                             'cloud' is for a provider-managed VPS: BIAB then
                             never writes an sshd drop-in, never enables
                             password auth and never binds sshd to the tailnet.
                             Persisted on first install; survives biab update.
  --lang=<en|es>             Language of the setup screens (default: ask, else en).
                             Persisted on first install; `biab lang` changes it.
  --force                    Reset wizard-phase state so the wizard runs again.
                             Does not reinstall the stack.
  --skip-wizard              Install the stack and exit (no OAuth steps).
                             Useful for CI / image baking.
  --non-interactive          Read BIB_USER, BIB_NAME, BIB_FLAVOR, BIB_AI_CLI
                             from the environment. Fail fast if any required
                             var is missing. Used by CI and autoinstall.
  --update                   Re-run idempotently on a box that already went
                             through install once. Skips completed phases.
  --uninstall                Remove everything BIAB-owned and exit.
                             Leaves user home, Tailscale, gh, Claude auth.
  --selftest                 Run the personal-refs guard against the install
                             tree and verify state.json schema; exit.
  --latest                   With --update or --skip-wizard: install the newest
                             stable upstream versions instead of the tested pins.
                             Untested and unsupported; `biab update` returns.
  --auto-update on [schedule] | off | status
                             The opt-in update timer (never uses --latest).
  --i-know-what-im-doing     Continue even if the OS is not Ubuntu 24.04.
  -h, --help                 Show this help.
[rc=0]

=== preflight-ack
[TS] WARN: installing over SSH with no private network up yet (BIB_SSH_INSTALL_ACK=1 set, continuing)
[rc=0]
=== preflight-noninteractive

⚠ You are installing over an SSH connection and the private network
  (Tailscale) is not up yet. Later in setup, SSH gets restricted to that
  private network only — if this session is not reachable over it, you
  will be locked out.

  Expected and safe on a VPS: the wizard hardens to key-only first and
  never locks you out mid-session. NOT safe inside a console-less VM
  (e.g. multipass, whose shell is itself SSH) — that is not supported.
  Use a hypervisor with a real console instead (VirtualBox, UTM,
  virt-manager/Proxmox).

[TS] ERROR: no tty to confirm from (or --non-interactive). Set BIB_SSH_INSTALL_ACK=1 if you understand the risk, or install from a console.
[rc=1]
=== end
